digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate — LLM judge reliability measurement
propositions: The Pass-2/Pass-3 judge exhibits self-consistency drift across repeated evaluations of the same findings, introducing noise into the Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary that downstream gates R5 and R3 depend on.

Section-order permutation of input plan text causes the gate verdict to flip between PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE, violating the assumption that order-independent absolute rubric scoring is sufficient to eliminate order sensitivity.

Experiment A measures self-consistency of the agentic judge over 50 sampled findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort (the R5 routing set) using 3-vote Fleiss' κ and raw agreement, with pass floor κ≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8.

Experiment B measures order-shuffle stability of the gate verdict over 14 permutable plans (≥3 top-level sections) using 3 distinct section-order permutations per plan, with pass floor κ≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8 on the verdict categories.

Infra-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (marked by coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed) are excluded and re-run as execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, keeping only genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (neither flag present) in the agreement metric.

E6 is a pure measurement harness over the existing gate with no src/rebar code changes; its verdicts gate downstream stories R5 (self-consistency pass → proceed) and R3 (order-shuffle pass → proceed).
